Summary.SummarizedSegment: Patient presents for follow-up of hypertension. Reports intermittent frontal headaches over two weeks, worse in the afternoon, with minimal relief from over-the-counter ibuprofen. Home blood pressure around 145/92 mmHg. Denies chest pain, visual changes, nausea, or vomiting.
Vitals: BP 142/90 mmHg, HR 78, Temp 98.6F, RR 16, SpO2 99% RA. Alert, no acute distress. Cardiovascular: regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Neuro: cranial nerves II-XII intact, no focal deficits.
1. Essential hypertension, suboptimally controlled. 2. Tension-type headache, likely related to blood pressure. 3. Hyperlipidemia, stable.
Increase lisinopril to 20 mg daily. Continue atorvastatin. Home BP log. Basic metabolic panel and lipid panel. Follow up in 4 weeks.

AfterVisitSummary.SummarizedSegment: We discussed your blood pressure and headaches. Your lisinopril is being increased to 20 mg once daily. Please keep a home blood pressure log and return in 4 weeks. Call the clinic if headaches worsen or you develop chest pain or vision changes.

TranscriptSegments.Content: Good morning. How have your headaches been?
